claims.value: The design is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620, released 2026-06-17, with structured-source capture SRDB 2.3.4 captured 2026-07-11. The cycle model is 54 minutes from local fire-wave impact to the next impact. Creepy Jar has not published an official numerical phase formula; the value is strongly corroborated by the current starrupture.tools client and an independent runtime-reading open-source mod, so it must remain a versioned community/game-data model rather than an eternal invariant. Confidence states are Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, and Cycle data changed - re-sync required. Do not invent numerical accuracy; downgrade confidence after a large correction, device-clock change, model-version change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop. Until live validation is complete, use predicted, expected, favorable, and lower threat—not exact, safe, or guaranteed.

claims.value: Preserve the 54-minute engine model while presenting five player-meaningful states: Fire wave 0:00-0:30 (remain sheltered), Cooling 0:30-1:30 (remain sheltered), Recovery / quiet window 1:30-11:30 (lower ambient threat; use the window), World active 11:30-51:30 (ordinary enemies and ecology active), and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00 (return, bank loot, and shelter). Manual synchronization anchors 0:00 when the fire wall reaches the player. The no-scroll portrait hierarchy is: sync/capability and degraded-state line; semantic hero state with a huge monospaced countdown and explicit target; threat label plus one action sentence; at most two opportunity cards; then exact-time next events with Mute one cycle and Re-sync. During recovery, the hero counts down to when ordinary Vermin are expected to return; during normal ecology, it targets the next Ruptura or warning start. Keep a proportional whole-cycle rail for orientation, but also use minimum-width labeled steps or a next-events list so short Fire and Cooling phases remain legible. Color is supporting atmosphere and must be accompanied by text, symbols, and borders.

claims.value: Opportunity guidance is a separately versioned OpportunityWindow data model with id, start event or offset, end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. It must not be hardcoded into phase mechanics: enemy-return events and gathering windows are separate facts even when they currently align with phase boundaries. Initial evidence-backed card proposals are reduced ordinary POI population during Recovery with the caveat that triggered encounters may persist; Oxallop in early recovery while lakebeds are dry; cave access, Quartz, and Glowcaps during Recovery without guaranteed respawn; Ignitium immediately after Cooling through Recovery with variable spawn rate; Star Tears in late Recovery as experimental timing; Coralion/Vulpir eggs post-wave with variable spawn; surface foliage and water during regrowth/active world without exact species timing; and Sulheart hidden until validated. Surface the Ignitium/Star Tears tradeoff because community evidence indicates Star Tears mature on unharvested cooled Ignitium. Show at most two pinned cards, each with its expected window, caveat, and visible provenance such as confirmed, community-derived, player-observed, or experimental.

claims.value: Enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptics and must never rely on color or audio alone. The proposed enemy-return ladder is 5 minutes (amber edge, finish/leave hard POIs, short double haptic and optional tone, normal notification), 2 minutes (persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, optional notification), 1 minute (red instruction and emphasized seconds, stronger distinct cue, background alert off by default), 15 seconds (static danger border, large seconds, one final cue with no ticking), and the event (ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING, urgent triple cue, notification or explicitly armed alarm). Pre-Ruptura cues are optional 10 minutes, 5 minutes, warning start at 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact; an exit buffer may instead trigger TURN BACK NOW. Profiles are Full, Haptic only, and Visual only, with separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, Mute one cycle, and pre-session preview. Never replay missed cues after resume; collapse them to the strongest current-state message. Store absolute timestamps, recompute `(now - anchor) modulo cycle duration` on resume, reschedule after anchor/model/policy changes, and deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and restore it; do not use background audio as keep-alive. Live Activity covers only the armed next event. AlarmKit loud behavior requires per-app authorization and an explicit Arm action; never silently create endless 54-minute alarms. Earlier iOS uses normal notifications, Time Sensitive is opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Accessibility requires text/symbol/border or pattern alongside color, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, no flashing transition, no default per-second ticking, a stable VoiceOver sentence, visible capability state, and an exact Next alert time.

claims.value: Mission Timeline is the selected visual source of truth. The player-facing 54-minute sequence is Fire wave `0:00-0:30` (“Remain sheltered”), Cooling `0:30-1:30` (“Remain sheltered”), Recovery / quiet window `1:30-11:30` (“Lower ambient threat; use the window”), World active `11:30-51:30` (“Ordinary enemies and ecology active”), and Ruptura warning `51:30-54:00` (“Return, bank loot, and shelter”). The hero counts to the next meaningful event rather than elapsed time: cooling begins during Fire wave, recovery begins during Cooling, ordinary Vermin expected return during Recovery, warning start during World active, and impact during Ruptura warning. claims.value: Opportunities are evidence-bearing `OpportunityWindow` data—not phase mechanics or hardcoded view prose—with an ID, independent start/end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class/confidence, applicable game build, and source snapshot. claims.value: Alerts must distinguish enemy return from Ruptura through text/visuals plus distinct sounds and haptics, never color or audio alone. Enemy-return defaults are 5 minutes, 2 minutes, 1 minute, 15 seconds, and event; Ruptura supports optional 10 minutes, then 5 minutes, 2:30 warning start, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Preserve `Full`, `Haptic only`, and `Visual only`, category toggles, preview, visible `Mute one cycle`, and an exact `Next alert at …` capability check. Schedule notifications at absolute dates and replace them after anchor/model/policy changes; deduplicate by sync epoch/definition/event/cycle. Never replay missed cues: resume or clock correction emits no historical thresholds and reconciles to current state; foreground cues are fresh only through `5_000` milliseconds, and delayed crossings collapse to the latest fresh threshold. Pause schedules no alerts. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and restore it afterward; do not use background audio as keep-alive. A Live Activity may represent only the currently armed event. AlarmKit loud behavior is iOS 26-only, requires authorization and explicit player arming, and must not create an endless 54-minute alarm; earlier systems use normal local notifications, Time Sensitive is separately opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Also avoid flashing red, default per-second ticking, and per-second VoiceOver announcements; support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Reduce Motion.
